text:
aj: seeing a sharp p99 spike on hosted-api around 16:20 UTC, p95 also up ~120ms. not global but concentrated on a handful of hosts. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/hosted-api

maya: looking now. queue depth on those hosts jumped from ~4->18 for short-lived requests, rate limiter shows retries increasing. any recent rollout?

aj: no user-facing deploys 16:00-16:30. last infra change was the kernel-selector tweak earlier this week.

josh_b: profiler attached (cpu samples, aggregated):
```
# top samples
runtime::kernel_aux 44%
runtime::batch_path_slow 23%
runtime::kv_cache_eviction 12%
other 21%
```
This smells like kernel selector falling back to aux kernels + batch slow path under weird batching distribution.

lara: we also have elevated KV cache evictions on the same hosts. eviction rate spiked at the same time as queue depth. tenant fingerprints look noisy: tenant_t-87 had bursty short requests (priming).

maya: confirmed. KV prefix hit-rate down from 98% -> 68% on hosts A,B. Prefetch backlog counters show a 3x increase.

aj: could noisy tenant priming force prefetch churn and push batches into aux kernels? how does kernel selector decide?

josh_b: kernel selector picks path based on predicted sequence length + batch size distribution. If batch sampler sees many single-token requests it moves to a less-optimized kernel to avoid OOM/latency tail, which hurts multi-token requests. With KV evictions, requests lose prefix caching and become longer to compute -> feedback loop.

sam-runtime: quick mitigation options: 1) isolate tenant_t-87 with a temporary tenant rate limit (throttle priming) 2) bump batch_sampler min-size threshold so we don't flip kernel for brief jitter 3) pin affected hosts to primary kernel via runtime flag. which do we want to try first?

lara: I can push a soft rate cap on tenant_t-87 (10r/s) for 10m. that should reduce prefix churn.

aj: do it. also please add a rule to mark those hosts to prefer primary kernel (runtime flag) while we investigate.

deploy-bot: rollback of kernel-selector heuristic (canary) requested by lara. Rollback job queued: job-id=rb-202633-11, started

maya: after soft cap + rollback canary, p99 dropped ~60ms within 90s and queue depth settled back near baseline. KV hit-rate slowly recovering.

josh_b: got a flamegraph capture post-rollback, aux kernel samples down to 7%. still seeing small # of batch_slow samples but within normal variance. attaching note: follow-up to tune sampler hysteresis and prefetch backoff to avoid flip-flop.

aj: good. action items: 
- lara: keep tenant cap for 30m then reassess (done)
- josh_b: create a small PR to add hysteresis to batch_sampler + unit tests (link when ready)
- maya: add an alert compound rule: if kv_eviction_rate > 5% AND aux_kernel_pct > 15% -> page oncall (right now we only alert on each individually)
- sam-runtime: draft runtime flag doc for kernel pinning and tenant isolation playbook

lara: noted and monitoring. will post updates if anything pops up. :thumbsup:

aj: thanks team, keeping this thread as the incident record. closing once we have PR + alert change merged.

maya: small note for postmortem: consider adding per-tenant sampling of sequence length distribution to feed kernel selector, today we use cluster-wide histograms which hide noisy tenants.

josh_b: agreed. I'll include perf numbers in the PR.

deploy-bot: rollback job rb-202633-11 completed successfully on hosts A,B,C at 16:25 UTC.

aj: p99 back to baseline at 16:27, leaving tenant cap active for 25m. thanks everyone.
